mainEntity.name: What is the difference between HEPA and ULPA filters?

acceptedAnswer.text: HEPA filters capture 99.95-99.995% of particles at 0.3 microns. ULPA filters capture 99.9995% at 0.12 microns. ULPA is used for ISO Class 3-4 cleanrooms; HEPA for ISO Class 5-8.

mainEntity.name: What is the price of a HEPA filter in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: HEPA filter price in India ranges from ₹3,500 to ₹8,500 for standard 610x610mm size depending on grade (H13 vs H14). Mini pleat HEPA filters cost ₹4,200-₹6,000. Call +91 8484 836 337 for exact pricing.

mainEntity.name: Can HEPA filters be washed and reused?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. HEPA filters are made of micro glass fiber paper and washing destroys the media. HEPA filters must be replaced, not washed.

mainEntity.name: How often should air filters be replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pre-filters: 1-3 months. Fine filters: 3-6 months. HEPA filters: When pressure drop reaches 2x initial (typically 3-5 years) or annual DOP test failure.

mainEntity.name: What are the different types of air filters available?

acceptedAnswer.text: Main air filters types include: Pre-filters (G4), Fine/Bag Filters (M5-F8), HEPA Filters (H13-H14), ULPA Filters (U15-U16), and Mini Pleat HEPA Filters.

mainEntity.name: What is a mini pleat HEPA filter?

acceptedAnswer.text: A mini pleat HEPA filter uses multiple pleats to maximize surface area in a compact 75mm deep frame. Efficiency is 99.997% at 0.3 microns – same as standard HEPA but 60% smaller.

mainEntity.name: What is the efficiency of H13 vs H14 HEPA filters?

acceptedAnswer.text: H13 efficiency: 99.95% at 0.3 microns. H14 efficiency: 99.995% at 0.3 microns. H14 is required for pharmaceutical sterile manufacturing.

mainEntity.name: What sizes of HEPA filters are available?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard sizes: 305x305mm, 610x305mm, 610x610mm, 915x760mm, 1220x610mm, 1220x915mm. Custom sizes available.

mainEntity.name: What is the pressure drop of a HEPA filter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Initial pressure drop: 25mm of WC. Final pressure drop (replace at): 50-70mm of WC. Replace when pressure drop doubles.

mainEntity.name: What material is used for HEPA filter frames?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frame materials include Aluminum Extruded Profile (most common), GI (Galvanized Iron), and SS 304 (pharma grade).

mainEntity.name: What is the price of a biosafety cabinet in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Biosafety cabinet price in India ranges from ₹2.5 lakh to ₹4 lakh for Class I, ₹4 lakh to ₹8 lakh for Class II Type A2, and ₹8 lakh to ₹14 lakh for Class II Type B2. Class III cabinets require custom pricing. Factors affecting price include size (2ft, 4ft, or 6ft), material (SS 304 vs MS), filter grade (H13 vs H14), and certification requirements. GeM portal lists Class II cabinets starting at ₹2,99,900. Call +91 8484 836 337 for exact pricing.

mainEntity.name: What are the different types of biological safety cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main biological safety cabinets types are Class I (personnel protection only), Class II (personnel, product, and environmental protection) with subtypes A1, A2, B1, B2, and Class III (gas-tight glove box for maximum containment). Class II Type A2 is the most common for microbiology and pharmaceutical labs, recirculating 70% of air and exhausting 30%.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a biosafety cabinet and a laminar flow hood?

acceptedAnswer.text: A laminar flow hood provides only product protection by blowing HEPA-filtered air over the work surface. A biosafety cabinet provides three layers of protection: personnel (inward airflow barrier), product (HEPA-filtered downflow), and environment (HEPA-filtered exhaust). Never use a laminar flow hood for infectious agents as it does not protect the user.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Class II Type A2 and Type B2 biosafety cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Class II Type A2 recirculates 70% of air and exhausts 30% back into the laboratory through a HEPA filter. Class II Type B2 exhausts 100% of air through hard ducting to the outside, making it suitable for chemical and cytotoxic drug work. Type B2 requires dedicated building exhaust and is more expensive to install and operate.

mainEntity.name: What is the working principle of a biosafety cabinet?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biosafety cabinet working principle involves three layers of HEPA-filtered airflow. Room air is drawn through the front grille at 100 fpm for personnel protection. HEPA-filtered air flows downward over the work surface at 55 fpm for product protection. Exhaust air passes through another HEPA filter before recirculation or exhaust for environmental protection.

mainEntity.name: How does a biosafety cabinet HEPA filter work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biosafety cabinet HEPA filter uses three mechanisms to capture particles: impaction for large particles, interception for medium particles, and diffusion for very small particles. HEPA filters achieve 99.99% efficiency at 0.3 microns (H14 grade). Some cabinets use ULPA filters with 99.999% efficiency at 0.12 microns for ISO Class 3 work zones.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Class II biosafety cabinet cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Class II Type A2 biosafety cabinet price ranges from ₹4 lakh to ₹8 lakh depending on size (3ft, 4ft, or 6ft) and manufacturer. Type B2 cabinets cost ₹8 lakh to ₹14 lakh due to hard ducting requirements. Servo brand Class II cabinets start at ₹1,85,000, while Esco cabinets range from ₹4,50,000 upwards. Custom sizes and SS 316 construction cost more.

mainEntity.name: What are the standard biosafety cabinet sizes available?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard biosafety cabinet sizes are 2ft (600mm work width), 3ft (900mm), 4ft (1200mm), and 6ft (1800mm). External dimensions for a 4ft cabinet are approximately 1200 x 750 x 1200 mm. Government tender specifications require B2 cabinets with external size 1800 x 850 x 2500 mm for 6ft models. Custom sizes available on request.

mainEntity.name: What is the function of a biosafety cabinet?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary biosafety cabinet function is to provide three layers of protection: personnel protection (operator from infectious aerosols), product protection (samples from airborne contamination), and environmental protection (preventing release of biological agents into the laboratory or outside). This triple protection is mandatory for BSL-2, BSL-3, and BSL-4 work.

acceptedAnswer.text: Leading biosafety cabinet manufacturers in India include Peter Air Systems (Mumbai), Alphalinear, Bio-Clean Air Devices and Services (Chennai), Servo Enterprises (Chennai), and Discovery Bionics (Delhi). Peter Air Systems offers in-house manufacturing with SS 304 construction, H14 HEPA filters, and pan-India installation and certification services.

acceptedAnswer.text: A supply diffuser and return differ in airflow direction: supply diffusers blow conditioned air INTO a room with adjustable louvers, while return diffusers draw used air OUT with fixed open grilles (90% free area). Combined units do both.

mainEntity.name: How does an HVAC air diffuser improve indoor comfort?

acceptedAnswer.text: An HVAC air diffuser spreads air horizontally across the ceiling using the Coanda effect, preventing drafts on occupants. This creates uniform temperature without hot or cold spots compared to standard grilles.

mainEntity.name: What size diffuser do I need for my room?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard guideline: 1 CFM per square foot of room area. A 200 sq ft room needs ~200 CFM. For 200 CFM, a 450x450 mm diffuser is typically sufficient. Our technical team can calculate exactly for your space.

mainEntity.name: What is the typical supply return air diffuser price in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: GI powder coated diffusers cost ₹350-₹1,200 depending on size. SS 304 diffusers for pharma applications cost ₹1,500-₹5,500. Combined supply/return units cost ₹3,500-₹5,500 for 600x600 mm. Call +91 8484 836 337 for bulk pricing.

mainEntity.name: Are energy-efficient diffusers worth the extra cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Energy-efficient diffusers with low pressure drop design can reduce fan energy consumption by 15-30%, typically paying back the additional cost within 6-12 months.

mainEntity.name: How noisy are ceiling diffusers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our low noise air diffusers operate at NC 25-35 depending on airflow, which is quieter than a library (NC 35-40). NC 25 is whisper-quiet and suitable for bedrooms and recording studios.

mainEntity.name: Can I paint my air diffuser to match my ceiling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. GI powder coated diffusers can be repainted with acrylic paint. However, we recommend ordering custom RAL colors from us for factory finish. Avoid painting over louvers as it may affect their movement.

mainEntity.name: How often should air diffusers be cleaned?

acceptedAnswer.text: Monthly dusting, quarterly deep cleaning (remove face and vacuum), annual professional inspection. In cleanrooms, follow your validated cleaning protocol. Residential diffusers can be cleaned every 3-6 months.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a diffuser and a register?

acceptedAnswer.text: A diffuser has adjustable louvers to direct airflow in multiple directions (2-way, 3-way, or 4-way). A register has a fixed damper but is otherwise similar. A grille has no damper and is used only for return air.

mainEntity.name: What is the function of a return air riser in HVAC?

acceptedAnswer.text: The return air riser function is to carry used or stale air from occupied spaces back to the Air Handling Unit (AHU) for reconditioning. This maintains air pressure balance, improves indoor air quality, and saves energy by recirculating conditioned air.

mainEntity.name: How is a return air duct riser different from a supply air riser?

acceptedAnswer.text: A return air duct riser carries air FROM rooms TO the AHU. A supply air riser carries conditioned air FROM the AHU TO rooms. Both work together in a balanced HVAC system.

mainEntity.name: How to add a return air duct to an existing building?

acceptedAnswer.text: Adding a return air duct requires: airflow calculation, path planning, fabrication of custom riser sections, installation of support framework, connection to AHU, and testing. Peter Air offers professional installation services across India.

mainEntity.name: What materials are return air risers made from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common materials include GI (Galvanized Iron) powder coated, SS 304 stainless steel (pharma grade), and MS (Mild Steel) powder coated. Each has different cost and application benefits.

mainEntity.name: What is the typical return air riser price in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: GI powder coated risers cost ₹6,000-₹8,000 per piece. SS 304 risers for pharma applications cost ₹15,000-₹25,000 per piece. Custom sizes are quoted separately. Call +91 8484 836 337 for exact pricing.

mainEntity.name: Can a return air riser include a HEPA filter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For cleanroom and pharmaceutical applications, we offer return air risers with integrated HEPA filters. These include DOP test ports and differential pressure ports for filter monitoring.

mainEntity.name: How do you maintain a return air riser?

acceptedAnswer.text: Monthly: inspect grill and check for noises. Quarterly: clean pre-filters and check for leaks. Annually: replace HEPA filters (if applicable) and conduct airflow testing. AMC options available.

mainEntity.name: Are return air risers customizable for specific projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We offer complete customization – material, size, filter type, damper type, grill finish, and dimensions. Our team works from your drawings or we can design based on site requirements.

mainEntity.name: What industries use return air risers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pharmaceutical cleanrooms, hospitals (OTs, ICUs), commercial buildings (offices, malls), industrial manufacturing, food processing, data centers, and telecom exchanges.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide installation across India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Peter Air serves clients across India with on-site installation support. Major cities have dedicated service teams with 48-hour response time.

mainEntity.name: What warranty do you offer on return air risers?

acceptedAnswer.text: 1 year comprehensive warranty covering manufacturing defects, material quality, and workmanship. Extended warranty available with AMC.

mainEntity.name: How does a return air riser help with energy efficiency?

acceptedAnswer.text: By recirculating conditioned air instead of exhausting it, return air risers reduce the load on your HVAC system, leading to 20-30% energy savings compared to systems without proper return air paths.
